## Format

> Source for all rules below: the journal's instructions for authors, https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf (live, "Last revised on 26 June 2023"; retrieved 2026-11-23). The same limits are repeated in the call-for-papers text of the journal page (Wayback copy 2026-10-17).

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research articles and review essays, plus short critical book reviews; introductions, forewords and prefaces are named in the length rule. Crossref and OpenAlex counts show book reviews are a large share of items (29 of 152 OpenAlex records, 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit** | Research article up to 8,000 words including quotations and footnotes; review essay up to 6,000; book review, introduction, foreword or preface up to 2,000 |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The instructions state the limits without any exception clause |
| **Abstract limit** | English abstract of up to 150 words for research articles and review essays; 5-6 lower-case keywords; a short title of no more than 6 words for the running head |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap. Footnotes (not endnotes) with full references in the notes and none in the body, following the Chicago Manual of Style; the footnotes count inside the 8,000 words |
| **Supplementary material** | Not addressed except figures: separate source files (jpeg, png or tif, not PDF), at least 300 dpi, 600 dpi for line art |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit stated; resolution minimum above |
| **Language and script** | American English; an English translation of every quotation in another language; Unicode fonts; pinyin for all Chinese texts and names, with traditional-form characters at first mention only; Daoism not Taoism; BCE/CE. A non-native writer's manuscript must be proof-read by a native English reader with subject knowledge, whose name goes in the initial submission |
| **Submission route** | By e-mail to the editors named in the instructions (the PDF names the late editor-in-chief and the managing editor); the call text of the journal page says the same ("sent via e-mail unless advised differently"). No online submission system link was found on the page read |

### Orientation

> Counts below come from Crossref records of this journal published 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 190 records, of which 122 (64.2%) carry an abstract (none of the 31 titles containing "written by" do). Shares use the 122 abstract-bearing records as denominator and match title plus abstract text, case-insensitive, with the exact regex given in each row (word boundaries; `(?-i:` marks a case-sensitive part). Counts are lower bounds. Retrieved 2026-11-23 from https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0301-8121,from-pub-date:2021-01-01,until-pub-date:2026-11-23 (cursor paging).

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Theoretical and textual: `\b(?:conceptual|theoretical|reconstruct(?:s|ion|ive)?)\b` 9 (7.4%); `\bhermeneutic(?:s|al)?\b` 16.4% (20); `\btranslat(?:e|es|ed|ion|ions|ing)\b` 15 (12.3%). Empirical vocabulary is rare: `\b(?:quantitative|statistic(?:s|al)?|survey|questionnaire|experiment(?:al|s)?|empirical(?:ly)?)\b` 4 (3.3%) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Neither is a normal mode here: `\b(?:interview(?:s)?|ethnograph(?:y|ic)|fieldwork|qualitative)\b` 0 of 122; the quantitative pattern above 4 of 122 |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Mostly within philosophy, religion and intellectual history of China; the stated scope lists four historical periods and five fields (logic and scientific thinking, metaphysics, moral philosophy and philosophy of religion, art theories and aesthetics, social and political philosophies) and explicitly welcomes comparison with Western schools (journal page, Wayback copy 2026-10-17). `\b(?:comparative|comparison|compare(?:s|d)?)\b` 15 (12.3%); `\b(?:ecolog(?:y|ical)|environment(?:al)?|climate)\b` 3 (2.5%); `(?-i:\bAI\b)|\bartificial intelligence\b|\bChatGPT\b` 1 (0.8%) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Scope condition stated by the journal: contributions are invited in the stated periods and fields from anyone seriously interested in Chinese philosophy "regardless of their orientation"; the instructions add that a submission failing the stated requirements does not enter review (instructions PDF, https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf, 2023-06-26; journal page Wayback copy 2026-10-17).
- **What kind of engagement?** Chinese philosophy as the object, treated with "critical and rigorous methodology of analysis, organization, and synthesis" (journal page, https://web.archive.org/web/20261017131533/https://brill.com/view/journals/jcph/jcph-overview.xml) and clear argument; comparison with Western schools is welcomed. Special attention is promised to "articles dealing with narrow topics with broad significance" (https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf).
- **Article type and length**: research article up to 8,000 words, review essay 6,000, book review 2,000, abstract up to 150 words, 5-6 keywords, Chicago-style footnotes (https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf; Format section).
- **Language framing rules**: pinyin for Chinese terms, traditional characters at first mention only, English translation of all foreign-language quotations, native-speaker proof-reading with the reader named (https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: a manuscript that does not meet the stated requirements "would not enter the review stage" (instructions PDF). Beyond that, blank: no desk-rejection data exists (SciRev, https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-chinese-philosophy/, has no reviews).

### Methodological Preferences

> Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share of the 122 abstract-bearing Crossref records (2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23, of 190 records) matching the regex in title or abstract; 0 hits = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. Regexes are case-insensitive with word boundaries, written in the Orientation section. ### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Sample: of the 122 abstracts, 60 contain a first-person form: `\b(I|my)\b(?! (?:Am|Ching))` (case-sensitive) matches 47 and `\b(we|our)\b` (case-sensitive) matches 23, overlapping; plural "we" may be generic and the "I" pattern can match a Roman numeral, so these are upper bounds. A narrower pattern `\bI (?:argue|examine|show|contend|suggest|propose|will|claim|explore|discuss|defend|seek|aim|analy[sz]e|maintain|offer|present)\b` matches 30 of 122 (24.6%). The most recent abstracts use "I argue" and "I examine", e.g. https://doi.org/10.1163/15406253-12340182 and https://doi.org/10.1163/15406253-12340169. The instructions give no first-person rule (https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf) |
| **Expected density** | Length ceiling 8,000 words including quotations and footnotes for articles; 6,000 for review essays (https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf, 2023-06-26). Crossref page counts were not tallied |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Up to 150 words headed "Abstract"; 5-6 lower-case keywords headed "Keywords"; a running-head short title of no more than 6 words (https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf, 2023-06-26) |
| **Writing style notes** | American English; double quotation marks, with commas and stops placed inside; footnotes with full references in Chicago style and none in the body text; pinyin without tone marks and in italics; BCE/CE in small capitals; Chinese characters limited to 20 per phrase (https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf, 2023-06-26) |
| **Authorship pattern** | Of the 143 non-review Crossref records that carry an author list (2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23), 134 (93.7%) have one author, 6 (4.2%) two and 3 (2.1%) three; 16 further non-review records carry no author list (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0301-8121,from-pub-date:2021-01-01), retrieved 2026-11-23 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | No journal-specific rule. Brill's publication-ethics page requires authors using human subjects, medical or not, to confirm signed informed consent and to protect identities, and requires trial registration for medical trials (https://web.archive.org/web/20261112042919/https://brill.com/page/author_ethics, copy 2026-11-12). Work in this journal is almost entirely textual (empirical regex 4 of 122 abstracts) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | 134 of 143 non-review Crossref records with an author list are single-author (93.7%), 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0301-8121,from-pub-date:2021-01-01) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The instructions contain no affiliation rule or independent-scholar clause (https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/JCPH.pdf). A title page with full contact details of all authors is required |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Blank. No data-sharing statement in the instructions PDF |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind: names, affiliations and acknowledgements only on a separate title page; other files and document properties must be anonymised (instructions PDF, 2023-06-26). Self-archiving of the submitted version is allowed at any time under the publisher's rules (same PDF), which can reveal authorship |
| **AI use** | Language improvement only, documented in Materials and Methods or Acknowledgements; no AI authorship (https://web.archive.org/web/20261112042919/https://brill.com/page/author_ethics, copy 2026-11-12) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; Brill Open optional, general article price 2,400 EUR for articles up to 35 pages and 15,000 words (https://web.archive.org/web/20261112140027/https://brill.com/page/oa_pricing, copy 2026-11-12). No submission fee is mentioned in the instructions PDF |
| **Language support** | A non-native writer's manuscript must be proof-read by a native English reader with subject knowledge, named in the initial submission (instructions PDF, 2023-06-26) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the manuscript must be about Chinese philosophy or thought, in one of the four periods and five fields the journal lists, or comparative work anchored in it (Framing Requirements; journal page, Wayback copy 2026-10-17). A paper with no Chinese-philosophy subject is outside the stated scope.
- **Length**: research articles are capped at 8,000 words including quotations and footnotes; the instructions state no exception (Format; instructions PDF, 2023-06-26).
- **Anonymisation**: a manuscript with author names, affiliations or revealing file properties in the main files breaks the double-blind rule (Peer Review, Practical Concerns).
- **Requirements gate**: a submission that does not meet the stated requirements is not sent to review (Peer Review, Framing Requirements).
- **AI use**: AI beyond language improvement, or undocumented use, breaches Brill's policy and can lead to rejection or retraction (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Language and script work**: pinyin conventions, characters only at first mention, translated quotations and a named native-speaker proof-reader for non-native writers add preparation steps (Format; instructions PDF).
- **Citation format**: Chicago-style footnotes with full references and no in-text references (Format); a paper prepared in an author-date style has to be converted.
- **Time**: no review-time figure exists (Review Cycle Time blanks), so turnaround cannot be planned from evidence.
- **Editorial contact uncertainty**: the instructions name an editor-in-chief who is shown on the board page with dates ending in 2024 (Identity), so the current submission contact has to be confirmed with the publisher before sending.
- **Open-access cost**: gold open access carries a general Brill price of 2,400 EUR; the journal-specific figure was not found (Open Access).

### Best Suited For

- Interpretive, textual and comparative work on Confucian, Daoist and Buddhist thought: `Confuci-` 28.7%, Daoist terms 22.1%, hermeneutic 16.4%, comparative 12.3% of 122 abstracts (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Annotated translations of primary texts: translation of primary materials is the first of the journal's three stated efforts, and 12.3% of abstracts mention translation (Framing Requirements, Methodological Preferences).
- Single-authored essays: 134 of 143 non-review records with an author list are single-author (Voice & Style).
- Comparative papers that read Chinese thought against Western figures: 23.8% of abstracts name a Western philosopher from the pattern (Epistemological & Political Leanings).

### Not Recommended For

- Empirical, interview-based or quantitative studies: quantitative vocabulary appears in 4 of 122 abstracts and interview or ethnography vocabulary in 0 (Methodological Preferences). This shows the form is absent, not that it would be rejected.
- Systematic reviews and meta-analyses: 0 of 122 abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Work on contemporary technology or AI: 1 of 122 abstracts (Sensitive Topics); absent from the topics, not evidence of rejection.
- Authors who need a published turnaround time or acceptance rate before choosing: none exists in any source read (Metrics, Review Cycle Time).
